title: Graceful stream termination and token reconciliation for Hosted API (reduce partial-output customer escalations)
creator: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary:
Multiple enterprise customers (notably AcmeHealth and CatalystShop) reported truncated/partial outputs from the Hosted API SSE stream. Symptoms: UI stuck waiting for final token, partial JSON blobs, and client-side retries producing duplicate content. Root cause appears to be a race between stream finalization and connection termination on edge proxies under transient load; KV cache flushes and response finalizer path sometimes run after socket close in our current async worker scheduling.

Why this ticket is unique:
Existing tickets focused on resume strategies and stitching (historical list includes several fixes). This work introduces a server-signed finalization marker and a compact sequence-based reconciliation protocol to make partial outputs deterministically replayable and safe for clients to resume/complete without duplication. It also covers a cross-environment compatibility plan (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) through feature-flagged behavior and a rollout matrix.

Reproduction notes (internal):
1) Use curl SSE endpoint with slow consumer: curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -N "https://api.hosted.example/v1/stream?model=rw-medium"
2) Under synthetic edge CPU pressure (loadgen 70% on edge), terminate the TCP connection at 95% token emission. Observe last SSE comment line missing finalization marker and client receives partial JSON.
3) Local repro harness: runtime/tests/stream/partial_repro.sh (linked in Confluence doc).

Investigation summary (timeline):
- 2026-03-04: Initial escalation from AcmeHealth; engineered workaround: client-side 7s idle-to-failback and re-request final-chunk via /v1/stream/finalize endpoint.
- 2026-03-05: Reproduced with loadgen; confirmed race window where finalizer callback executes after socket close.
- 2026-03-06: PoC: included explicit SSE comment "event: final
: final-marker: <sig>

". Works for clients that keep connection long enough, but fails when connection closed before marker send completes.

Design proposal (this ticket):
1) Introduce server-side finalization token embedded in every partial SSE chunk as a short sequence header comment: ":seq=1234 sig=ab12...
". The final chunk includes a signed final marker: ":final=1 sig=...
".
2) Persist the last N chunks' compact digest in the per-request ephemeral store (Redis or in-memory cache depending on deployment) for 30s to allow deterministic replay via a new idempotent POST /v1/stream/resume endpoint that accepts (request_id, last_seq, client_nonce) and returns missing fragments or a signed final token.
3) For Dedicated/Private: expose feature-flag to allow local cache backend (memcached/HW blob) and a config knob for retention TTL. Default behavior is backward-compatible: if resume endpoint not reachable, client falls back to previously implemented retry semantics.
4) Server guarantee: sequence numbers monotonic per-request; final signed marker proves completeness; signed markers use the same KMS-backed key used for audit signatures for tamper-resistance.

Mitigations already deployed:
- Short-term: edge route sticky to origin instance for 30s after stream start for affected customers (AcmeHealth). Implemented 2026-03-06 by infra team, reduced incidents but not a full fix.
- Client guidance: added recommended client behavior to docs: accept SSE comments with seq and tolerate reconnect attempts to /v1/stream/resume. Sent note to customers 2026-03-07.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement sequence header in runtime (C++ component), persist last-chunk digests to ephemeral cache, add resume endpoint microservice, unit+integration tests.
- Phase 2: signed final marker backed by KMS integration (coord with security), update SDKs to parse seq/final markers and call resume endpoint.
- Phase 3: canary rollout to 10% of Hosted traffic, monitor metrics, then 100% rollout and backport to Dedicated/Private packaging.

Testing and validation:
- Add deterministic unit tests for sequence monotonicity and final marker generation.
- Add integration test that kills TCP mid-stream and verifies resume endpoint returns final marker or missing fragments.
- Load test with the chaos harness (runtime/tests/load/chaos_stream_kill) at 5k RPS to validate no increased tail latency.
- E2E SDK test matrix across Node/Python/Java showing idempotent resume.

Rollout and observability:
- New metrics: stream_seq_restarts, stream_resume_success, stream_final_marker_miss. Add dashboards in Console under Streaming -> Resilience.
- Alerts: alert if stream_resume_success < 95% for 10m on canary.

Backward compatibility and customer migration:
- Clients that do not implement resume will continue to see partial outputs but can be offered opt-in sticky routing or manual retry.
- SDK patch releases will include resume logic and be paired with a migration guide.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Additional ephemeral storage increases memory/redis usage; we cap persisted per-request footprint to ~2KB and TTL default 30s.
- Signed final marker requires KMS access pattern; adds small latency at finalization path on hosted (estimated +3ms).

Links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stream+Finalization+Design
- PR (runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1542
- Microsvc PR (resume endpoint): https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-resume/pull/18
- Customer incident notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/ACME-STREAM-2026-03

Next steps (short):
- Marco to land runtime seq header PoC branch and open PR by 2026-03-10 (DONE: draft branch opened).
- QA to run integration repro and pass tests by 2026-03-14.
- Security to review KMS signing plan by 2026-03-11 (requested).

Acceptance criteria:
- Host runtime emits monotonic seq comments for every SSE chunk and stores compact digest of last N chunks for resume.
- Resume endpoint returns missing fragments or signed final marker within 200ms for typical requests.
- SDKs can use resume endpoint to produce identical output to uninterrupted stream without duplication.
comments: 2026-03-06 Marco Li: Opened runtime PoC branch 'feat/seq-header' and added test harness. Observed stable seq emission in unit tests.

2026-03-07 QA: Reproduced truncation locally with loadgen and verified that resume endpoint can replay final fragments in 80% of attempts; failure cases linked to race where digest not persisted due to Redis timeout (ticketed ENG-22367).
2026-03-08 PM (Jules Park): Notified AcmeHealth and CatalystShop about planned fix and timeline. They asked for a hotfix if canary fails.
2026-03-10 Security (R. Patel): Light review completed; KMS key reuse okay if we add rotation note. Full review scheduled for 2026-03-12.
2026-03-11 Marco Li: PR #1542 opened for code review. Integration tests failing in ephemeral store under high concurrency; experimenting with batching writes.
resolution_notes: Work in progress. PoC branch shows promise. Need to finalize eviction policy on ephemeral cache and finish KMS signing path. Customer mitigation (sticky routing) remains active for high-impact accounts.
approvals: Sofia Gomez - Eng Manager (approved for canary)
